headline: Postponed Harmony Dog Training kennel license renewal to October 7, 2026 amid neighbor noise and odor complaints.
summary: Neighbors of the Harmony kennel at 65 Patterson Avenue spoke about barking and odors, and the license holder described steps he has taken. The kennel renewal was postponed to October 7, 2026. Routine license petitions were approved, and a Tiki's Auto Sales Annex update was set for October 7, 2026.
decisions: Approved the records of the August 19, 2026 meeting as prepared by the Clerk.
Approved the consent agenda of routine license petitions on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved a one-day entertainment and premise expansion license for Rock's Bar at 451 Prospect Street on September 25, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved the request to change the business name from Wise Guys Deli to Leonardo's Pizza and Fried Chicken at 511 Broadway, on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved the Latinos Unidos de Rhode Island license for a Mexican Festival 2026 at 354 Pine Street on October 18, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.
Withdrew the RI Day of Portugal beer and wine license for a Taft Street block party at the applicant's request.
Read and placed on file objections to the Class A liquor license transfer for 368 Cottage Street.
Read and placed on file the Superior Court order appointing William J. Delaney as special master for City Boy LLC.
Approved the transfer of the automobile repair and second-hand shop license for 19 Benefit Street on a unanimous voice vote.
Withdrew the Class A liquor license transfer for 368 Cottage Street at the request of special master William J. Delaney, on a unanimous voice vote.
Continued the new auto repair shop license for Correia Auto Repair at 102 Esten Avenue to September 23, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.
Read and placed on file zoning inspection reports for Tiki's Auto Sales.
Scheduled a second update for Tiki's Auto Sales Annex at 772 Main Street for October 7, 2026.
Postponed the kennel license renewal for Harmony Dog Training at 65 Patterson Avenue to October 7, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.

A FORMAL HEARING , ORIGINALLY SCHEDULED FOR AUGUST 5, 2026, WAS 
TAKEN UP: 
 
KENNEL Renewal - 
 
Harmony (Harmony Dog Training LLC) 65 Patterson Ave. LIC#KNL-25-2 
 
Representing the City of Pawtucket was Frank J. Milos, Jr., Esq., City Solicitor. 
 
Attorney Milos read the alleged violations in summons, as follows:  
 
1. Nuisance Abatement – § 116-25(A); 
2. General Application Requirements – § 116-56(C) and § 410-60(U);  
3. General Licensing Requirements – § 116-59(K); and 
4. Noise Ordinance – § 286-10  
 
He stated that the focus of the hearing will be on the fact that the lot cannot be within 200 ft of 
a residential zone. 
 
Speaking on behalf of Harmony Dog Training LLC was attorney Amy H. Goins, Esq. , 
Ursillo, Teitz & Ritch, Ltd. 
 
Attorney Goins stated that Harmony had received approval from the Zoning Department.  She 
argued that the City cannot impose additional restrictions through the licensing process, as 
licensing should not be used to amend or circumvent zoning requirements. 
 
Attorney Goins further stated that she believed the summons to be insufficient because it did 
not identify specific allegations or violations. 
 
Attorney Milos stated that the points made by Ms. Goins are fair points.  He stated that he 
doesn’t like to proceed generally without specific dates, times or the event.  He noted that this 
matter is unique.  He stated that specific dates and issues should be identified, particularly in 
the event that the matter becomes litigious.  He noted that his questions for the hearing wer e 
based on reports, emails, and other documentation  that have been part of the record .  There 
are no secrets here.   Attorney Milos  requested one additional postponement to allow the 
attorneys sufficient time to review the matter. 
 
Councilor Mercer expressed the opinion that the matter should proceed that evening. 
 
Attorney Milos  disagreed with the assertion that the licensing process creates additional 
zoning issues. He stated that the City was not seeking to impose any additional zoning 
requirements or hurdles on the applicant. 
 
Speaking on behalf of the City was Carl Johnson, Director of Zoning and Code Enforcement, 
who was sworn in by City Clerk Richard J. Goldstein. 
 
Mr. Johnson stated that he issued a Zoning Compliance Certificate to Harmony Dog Trainin g 
LLC.  He explained that the property was located within two zoning districts: Residential -
Multi-Family and MO [Manufacturing Open].   He further explained that pursuant to §410-09, 
when a property is located in two zoning districts, the regulations of th e district comprising 
more than 50% of the property apply. Mr. Johnson stated that approximately 80% of the 
property is located within the MO zoning district.   He further stated that the kennel use was 
permitted by right in the MO zoning district ; therefor e, no special use permit , variance or 
other zoning relief was needed.  
 
Mr. Johnson stated that the additional requirements for licensing in section §410 -60 were not 
applicable to the issuance of the Zoning Compliance Certificate  because the use was allowe d 
by right.   
 
Upon questioning from Mr. Milos, Mr. Johnson stated that u nder §410 -60U3, the kennel 
cannot be within 200 feet of a residential district, commercial building or office building.
371 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
September 10, 2026 
Amended 
 
Because the kennel is partially located in a residential zone, it  cannot satisfy the required 200 
foot buffer requirement.  
 
Mr. Johnson explained that the Zoning Compliance Certificate was issued in accordance with 
the Zoning Ordinance. He fu rther stated that zoning inspection s are typically conducted after 
a Zoning Compliance Certificate has been issued and tha t inspections are for building, 
electrical, plumbing and health, and are  not for other zoning requirements, as the use was 
allowed by right. 
 
Councilor Mercer expressed the opinion that if there was an error in this matter , it was made 
by the City Council  regarding the licensing requirements rather than the Zoning Department  
for any Zoning requirements. 
 
Councilor Gregor stated that during the zoning application process, the ball was dropped  the 
process had failed. 
 
Upon questioning from Attorney Goins, Mr. Johnson stated that he has 13 years of experience 
serving as a zoning official.  He stated that the fitness of the applicant does not come into play 
when reviewing a request for a zoning certificate.  He also understands that zoning approvals 
run with the land. 
 
The next speaker was Elizabeth Sousa, 52 Vale Street, who was sworn in by City Clerk 
Richard J. Goldstein. 
 
Ms. Sousa stated t hat she lives at 52 Vale Street with her husband and daughter. She also 
stated that he daughter had a dog which has died. 
 
Ms. Sousa testified that initially a neighbor brought concerns regarding disturbances in the 
area to her attention; however, she thought it was a daycare and not an overnight kennel.  She 
stated that she subsequently heard barking early in the morning and late at night. 
 
Ms. Sousa stated that the barking had affected her daughter’s dog. 
 
She testified that, since January 25, when she has been in her backyard, she has heard barking 
as well as people yelling at the dogs. Although she is hard of hearing, she stated that the noise 
was loud enough for her to hear. 
 
Ms. Sousa stated that the kennel owner had installed soundproof windows, but s he could still 
hear the barking.   She further testified that for three weeks, starting at about 3:30 a.m. on a 
Sunday, she heard loud barking that continued into the morning. She stated that she was 
unsure whether anyone was present at the kennel at the time. 
 
Ms. Sousa stated that approximately one and a half weeks ago, she heard aggressive growling. 
She also stated that neighboring dogs respond to the dogs at the kennel. 
 
Ms. Sousa stated that she does not notice odors from the kennel, although she indica ted that a 
neighbor does. She expressed concern that the license should not have been approved so 
quickly and stated that the noise is constant. She also noted that a light at the property remains 
on 24 hours a day. 
 
 
The next speaker was Maddie Weeden, 64  Vale Street, who was sworn in by City Clerk 
Richard J. Goldstein. 
 
Ms. Weeden stated that she lives directly behind the kennel. She recalled that at the original 
hearing they were told that there would be no noise from the dogs because Mr. Rosado was a 
good trainer and that dog training was an art. She stated that in 2024, she testified that her 
concerns primarily involved noise and odors.   
 
She has three dogs, which are usually quiet, but are now responding to the dogs in the kennel . 
She stated that she contacted Animal Control to complain about the noise , which has been 
constant. She indicated that there had been no improvement with respect to the odors.
372 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
September 10, 2026 
Amended 
 
Ms. Weeden testified that th e noise conditions changed in 2025, but not for the better .  She 
stated that there have been no significant change s in 2026. She stated that odors remain an 
issue, although they were not as severe this summer as they were last summer.  She stated that 
there was a window with a hose that appear ed to discharge odorous air from the HVAC 
system. 
 
She stated that she was considering selling her home but a realtor advised that she would 
potentially lose money because of the issues associated with the kennel. 
 
She stated that in April 2026, she asked the Board not to renew the license or, alternatively, 
not to allow overnight boarding. 
 
Ms. Weeden also expressed concerns regarding the impact of the kennel on raising her child  
with that level of noise . She stated th at she would not have purchased the property had she 
known the kennel would be located there. 
 
Attorney Goins asked Ms. Weeden whether she had reviewed the zoning regulations when 
she purchased the property in 2023. 
 
Ms. Weeden responded “no.” 
 
She also st ated upon questioning from Ms. Goins that she did not have objections to the 
businesses that were there when she bought the house. 
 
Ms. Weeden stated that the problem lies with no buffer between her residential home and the 
kennel property.  She stated tha t there are approximately 34 feet between the properties  and 
not the required 200 feet.  She had video to show the board. 
 
Attorney Goins objected to the admission of audio and video evidence, stating that she had 
not been provided an opportunity to review the evidence. 
 
 
The next speaker was Kiara Whitsey, 45 Patterson Avenue, who was sworn in by City Clerk 
Richard J. Goldstein. 
 
Ms. Whitsey stated that she has lived at 45 Patterson Avenue since May 2023 and resides next 
door to the kennel. She testified t hat she first began experiencing significant noise from the 
kennel in May 2024. She stated that she contacted several City officials and testified before 
the Board in May 2024 regarding barking that occurred throughout the day. 
 
Ms. Whitsey stated that she spoke with the owner about the noise and was told that there was 
nothing he could do. She testified that the noise worsened in 2024, improved somewhat in 
mid-2025, and then escalated again in 2026.  She stated that the most recent incident occurred 
on August 23, when there was prolonged barking and she could hear people yelling at the 
dogs to be quiet. 
 
Ms. Whitsey also described the odors from the kennel as unbearable. She stated that she had 
tried various home remedies but had not experienced any improve ment. She expressed that 
she felt it was unfair to have to continue living under these conditions. 
 
Ms. Whits ey proposed changes to the hours of operation, including closing the kennel on 
weekends. 
 
She further stated that a new cleaning system was suppose d to be installed but that it had not 
resolved the odor issues. 
 
Ms. Whitsey stated that there is no buffer between her property and the kennel, only a chain -
link fence and not the required 200ft distance. 
 
In response to questions  from Attorney Goins, Ms. Whitsey stated that she had not reviewed 
the Zoning Ordinance or zoning map when she purchased the property.
373 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
September 10, 2026 
Amended 
 
The next speaker was license holder, Louis Rosado, 10 Jasmine Court, Cra nston, who was 
sworn in by City Clerk Richard J. Goldstein. 
 
Mr. Rosado stated that he began working at an animal hospital at the age of 15 and remained 
there for nine years. He has worked with animals ever since. He stated that he started 
Harmony in another city. 
 
Mr. Rosado stated that he spoke with Michelle  Hardy in the Clerk’s Office  regarding the 
location. He said that she initially told him twice that the location would not work, but on the
